- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and model shows gradual upward trend, cap upward bias by 5–10% if recent events show net supply deficit.
- If model forecast spikes sharply after a low, reduce forecast slope by 20–30% to avoid overshoot; especially if sentiment is mixed or bearish.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 3–5 consecutive days, apply mean reversion: next forecast = prior + 0.5*(true - prior) to avoid overconfidence.
- When official event balance is heavily bearish (net supply < -10) and sentiment is low, reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect supply shock.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows strong upward momentum, increase forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment is bullish and events are supply-constrained.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >15% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 15-day trend, not 30-day trend.
